articles.title: Marketing meltdown: why has Andrew Garfield’s new film suddenly added Robin Hood?
articles.summary: Paul Greengrass drama The Uprising was supposed to be a historical epic about the Peasants’ Revolt of 1381 – but a strange new campaign has inserted a surprising figure. Nobody likes to have the full plot of a movie spoiled before they’ve even seen it.
body: Here’s what we know so far. Initially, all the trailers and promotional materials made The Uprising look like a film about the Peasants’ Revolt that tore through England in 1381. And this was very exciting, since the revolt was a thrilling moment in history that has been bizarrely underserved by Hollywood over the years. Most excitingly of all, though, it sounded like it fit exactly into Greengrass’s wheelhouse; full of action and realism and political awareness.

But that all changed this week, when the film’s US distributor, Focus Features, announced the film’s full title on social media. What had once simply been The Uprising was now The Uprising: The Rise of Robin Hood. It added a new synopsis, reading: “Set against the true events of the Uprising that helped inspire the legend of Robin Hood, [Andrew Garfield’s character] forms an army of the people to face the King’s might in a fight for justice.”
points: Paul Greengrass drama The Uprising was supposed to be a historical epic about the Peasants’ Revolt of 1381 – but a strange new campaign has inserted a surprising figure.

articles.title: Plans in Development to Replace Edinburgh TV Festival as it Moves to Manchester
articles.summary: Scotland’s screen bodies are working on a new Edinburgh-based festival for the media and creative industries as the TV Festival moves to Manchester. Màiri McAllan Cabinet Secretary for Education, Culture and Gaelic confirmed the news at a launch event on the penultimate night of the festival.
body: Screen Scotland has already confirmed it will establish a new debate format, titled the Lynda Myles Debate, as part of the offering, named for Lynda Myles, formerly director of the EIFF and co-creator of the Edinburgh TV Festival.

“We are so proud of Scotland’s screen sector and this exciting addition to the August festivals line-up will provide a new way to embrace the creativity and cultural innovation which makes our capital unique,” said McAllan. “As a global hotbed of emerging talent, where new voices are heard and fresh stories are told, Edinburgh will continue its world-leading offer for the television industry with the support of the Scottish Government – and will do so alongside our other Edinburgh festivals, showcasing brilliance across artforms.”
Earlier this year the TV Festival, which celebrates its fiftieth anniversary this year, confirmed it would be moving to Manchester from 2027.

articles.summary: AncestryDNA is offering one of its steepest discounts of the year for Labor Day, giving amateur genealogists a cheaper way to uncover the kinds of family secrets that regularly leave celebrities stunned on PBS’ “Finding Your Roots.” Through Sept. 8 at 10 a.m.

Ancestry has an especially close connection to the celebrity-genealogy boom: the company is a corporate sponsor of PBS’ “Finding Your Roots,” Henry Louis Gates Jr.’s long-running series that combines historical records with DNA analysis to reconstruct the family trees of actors, musicians, athletes and other notable guests. Ancestry has also turned the show into a major piece of its own entertainment marketing, hosting episode recaps and celebrity clips and encouraging viewers to use its DNA tests and record database to conduct a DIY version of the research seen on screen.

Season 12, which aired earlier this year, included everyone from America Ferrera and Darren Criss to Lizzo, Flea, Spike Lee, Kristin Chenoweth, Brittney Griner and Chris Paul. Academy Award nominee David Hemingson (“The Holdovers,” “Kitchen Confidential”) is attached to adapt the murder mystery book and serve as…
body: “Set deep in the dense mountains of Vermont’s Northeast Kingdom, the series follows Ern Cunningham (Badgley), a mystery-writing expert who reluctantly attends a family reunion to welcome his brother Michael home from prison — the same brother Ern helped convict. When a frozen body appears and a snowstorm traps everyone inside, the deaths begin to mount. Everyone in his family has already killed someone – either by accident or otherwise.”
A limited series adaptation of the book was previously in development at HBO in 2022 with Made Up Stories and Fifth Season (then Endeavor Content) producing, though it ultimately did not go forward.

“We’re beyond excited to bring Ben’s sensational book to life in Dave Hemingson’s brilliant hands” said Papandrea and Hutensky. “We’ve found the perfect ‘Ern’ in Penn and it’s a dream to be making this series with our amazing partners Amazon MGM Studios and Fifth Season.”

articles.summary: CNN has apologized to the family of Dolly Parton after the news network incorrectly showed a photo on the air of a Dolly Parton tribute artist instead of the famed country singer herself. On Tuesday evening’s broadcast of CNN’s “Laura Coates Live” in the 11 p.m.
body: The Getty Images photo of Vohnn used by CNN ( above right ) was taken Dec. 16, 2025, in Las Vegas, where Vohnn was attending a screening of the movie “Song Sung Blue” at Brenden Theatres inside the Palms Casino Resort, according to the photo agency.

In an interview with the New York Post, which first reported on CNN’s apology over the mix-up, Vohnn said, “I started getting all these texts in from friends saying that I was on CNN, and I couldn’t believe it.” She continued, “I was already heartbroken at losing Dolly because of how much she has given to me as a woman and an artist. The photo of Vohnn appeared in a montage of images on “Laura Coates Live,” which featured five photos of the actual Dolly Parton.

articles.title: Robert Carlyle: ‘When we did The Full Monty strip, the reaction from the crowd was terrifying’
articles.summary: The actor on which star he’d devour first on a lifeboat, why he prefers pigeons to dogs and how Trainspotting put the Scottish accent on the map. You’re stranded on a lifeboat with Ewan McGregor, Ewen Bremner, Jonny Lee Miller, Kevin McKidd, Peter Mullan, James Cosmo, Keith Allen and Irvine Welsh.
body: I’m sure this will disappoint people, but there must have been 10 Wee Jocks. I just don’t like working with animals because they don’t know they’re acting, so it can take them 10 takes to cross a road. The best animals I’ve ever worked with were the pigeons on The Full Monty TV show, which we had to chase. I thought: “This is never going to work.” But they just did what they were told and would fly out of their box and land on your shoulder. I love pigeons now. Dogs, not so much.

What was it like to look in the mirror and see John Lennon staring back at you in Yesterday? MegMay I don’t particularly look like John Lennon, but apparently there’s something about the bridge of my nose that looks a bit like his, which is what the wonderful prosthetics people focused on. When they were putting it all on, I’d sunk quite low in the chair, so I could only see the top of my head in the mirror. When they finished and I sat up, it was quite freaky.

articles.title: Optimus Prime and Eeyore voice actor Peter Cullen dies
articles.summary: Cullen voiced the heroic Optimus Prime in the Transformers TV series and then the Hollywood films.
body: Actor Peter Cullen, who voiced popular characters including Optimus Prime in Transformers and Eeyore in Disney's Winnie the Pooh franchise, has died at the age of 85.

The Canadian actor began his most famous role - as the heroic deep-voiced Optimus Prime - for the Transformers TV series in 1984, then returned for seven Hollywood films from 2007 to 2023 and other spin-offs.
He voiced depressive donkey Eeyore in TV animation The New Adventures of Winnie the Pooh from the late 1980s as well as numerous related shows, films and games.

His other memorable voice parts included KARR, the evil counterpart to KITT in TV show Knight Rider; the clicking vocalisations of The Predator in Arnold Schwarzenegger's 1987 film; and the roars of King Kong in 1976.
points: Cullen voiced the heroic Optimus Prime in the Transformers TV series and then the Hollywood films.

articles.title: Colony review – zombies return to the mall with a fresh and frenzied range of scares
articles.summary: This time the ranks of the undead have acquired a hive mind, making them even more formidable adversaries. Can a maverick academic save the day? Here is another frenzied K-zombie action-horror from Yeon Sang-ho, the director of Train to Busan and Peninsula.
body: An upscale shopping mall occupies the lower floors of the tower, and it takes some nerve to give your zombie film much the same setting as Dawn of the Dead, the masterwork of the godfather of the genre George A Romero. Thankfully Colony can boast an innovation: these zombies have a hive mind, an emergent collective intelligence that makes them more formidable adversaries than your average braindead stumbler. The moment that one of the infected notices you and screams, as in Invasion of the Bodysnatchers, they all turn and attack.

And as they do, spasmodically jerking in unison, all angular limbs and unnatural angles, or while they writhe and entwine as they pile upon and devour their latest victim, the importance of movement choreographer Jeon Young is clearer than ever. A collaborator on each of Sang-ho’s zombie films, but this time working with a company of South Korea’s top contemporary dancers, Young makes many of the action and gore scenes resemble something you might see on stage at Sadler’s Wells. Michael Jackson’s Thriller video might have done it first but Colony does it better, more scarily and on an epic scale.

articles.title: ‘He could arch both eyebrows and curl his lips in every direction all at once’: Tim Curry’s five best screen roles
articles.summary: The actor fully embraced his physical talents and outsized personality with a line in theatrical baddies teetering deliciously on the edge of serious and silly. • Tim Curry, star of The Rocky Horror Picture Show and Stephen King’s It, dies aged 80 • Tim Curry on sexuality, surviving a stroke – and…
body: A physical actor bursting with personality, Curry was at his best inhabiting outsized roles. He near fills up the entire frame as the prowling Lord of Darkness who kidnaps a princess and torments innocent forest child Tom Cruise in Ridley Scott’s visually sumptuous high fantasy.

The debonair manner and hint of a self-amused smile that were seemingly Curry’s birthright were deployed to delightful effect as Wadsworth, the butler who is just about a half a step ahead of everyone else in this madcap murder-mystery comedy, reputedly worked on by Tom Stoppard, and inspired by the board game that’s called Clue in North America and Cluedo everywhere else.

Inculcating coulrophobia in an entire generation of kids who stayed up late to watch this TV Stephen King adaptation, Curry played a shapeshifting child-murdering interdimensional entity – but ever a devotee of the theatrical arts, he did it in clown makeup. Charming baddies were his metier, and Pennywise the Clown was the baddest of the lot.

articles.title: Blake Lively awarded $400,000 of $8m she claimed for legal fees in Baldoni battle
articles.summary: A judge awards less than Lively requested to cover her legal fees to fight a defamation case he filed.
body: Actress Blake Lively has been awarded $400,000 (£340,000) of the $8m (£6.9m) she tried to claim from her former co-star Justin Baldoni to cover her legal fees and costs to fight a defamation case he brought.
Lively initially sued Baldoni, her co-star and director of the 2024 film It Ends With Us for sexual harassment and retaliation, before he countersued for defamation.
A judge dismissed his defamation complaint in 2025, and she argued she was entitled to $7.5m (£6.4m) to cover her lawyers' fees and $540,000 (£460,000) for other costs.
But the judge said she should receive considerably less - a total of $407,451 - because she requested money for more people and time than were necessary to defend the defamation claim.
points: A judge awards less than Lively requested to cover her legal fees to fight a defamation case he filed.

articles.title: BBC director-general says he was not aware of 'severity' of cuts needed
articles.summary: Matt Brittin succeeded Tim Davie as boss of the BBC in May.
body: BBC director-general Matt Brittin has said he was not aware of the severity of the cuts the corporation needed to make when he took on his role.
Savings targets were announced in June, with planned cuts across news, nations and content divisions to deliver £160m of £500m in savings by the 2028-29 financial year.

Speaking at the Edinburgh TV Festival on Thursday, Brittin said: "On the financial side, I knew that cuts had been announced and that savings had been announced, but I hadn't really understood the severity."
There are expected to be around 2,000 jobs cut as part of the process.
